utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know whether we are prolonging our work today, and I may have a couple of questions. As far as I can tell, it won't take more than 10 to 15 minutes, but if this is put off until tomorrow, I may not have any questions if my turn comes after Mr. Olujic's.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Olujic, any questioning? Any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: At this point in time, we have no questions for this witness. Thank you. But if Madam Edina Residovic wishes to question the witness, I don't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's not the time now that matters, it's whether you have any cross-examination. If you have any cross-examination and it's not likely to be extensive, we can take your questions. Because it's not too much to continue for a few more minutes. So if you have any, let's have your questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: It says an error has occurred in your programme, to keep working anyway, check and ignore and save your work to quit. You will lose information you entered since your last save. I just don't want to lose anything. I haven't done anything except that thing has appeared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Residovic, let's hear you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Turkovic.

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm Defence counsel for Mr. Zejnil Delalic, and this time, this is correct, as opposed to a moment ago when there was an error in the translation. Mr. Turkovic, we do not know each other from before; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: No, that is not so. I saw you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That was my next question. We met for the first time, yesterday, briefly for fifteen minutes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the course of the examination-in-chief, you said that Senad Kazazic, the commander of the right bank had assigned you to the Musala facility; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In answer to a question, you said that this happened sometime in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: In June.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I may remind you, this was a couple of days after the unfortunate event that occurred when the Chetnik shell hit Musala?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I don't exactly know how many days afterwards but shortly afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we were to try to fix the time in relation to this event, then it must have been the second half of June of 1992; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Senad Kazazic was in 1992 -- let me rephrase my question. Mr. Senad Kazazic was the commander of the detachment, the detachment known as the right bank or Konjic 1?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: The right bank, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout the time you were at Musala, your immediate superior was Hebibovic known as Broceta?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Ismet Hebibovic known as Broceta, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout the time that Mr. Kazazic was in this detachment, Konjic 1, throughout that time he gave you advice regarding strict respect of the rights of the persons held in Musala?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kazazic insisted on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Turkovic, that you told me yesterday that you personally, never personally knew Mr. Zejnil Delalic, but that you had heard of him, like the other people of Konjic, especially on the basis of his discotheque?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Mr. Delalic was never a superior of yours while you were at Musala?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't, nor did he ever come to Musala.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you spent quite a bit of time in Musala, within the facility, while you were there?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, most of the time I slept there, unless I was on leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the detainees had the same food, same quality and quantity of food, as your soldiers did?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: That is true. Even during the conflict with the HVO, we would give them our food reserves. We set up a canteen, and the same cooks cooked for them and for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Turkovic, you said that a number of guards who provided security for Musala would occasionally go to the frontlines?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say that these were lines in the vicinity of the town of Konjic in the direction of the Chetnik positions, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct to say, Mr. Turkovic, that not a single of your guards was ever a member of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, no one was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Turkovic, thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Olujic, have you any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I said that I had no questions for this witness and I thank you. Not because of the time limit but simply I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. McHenry, any questions for you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has been speaking mostly about Musala. There's no allegations against them with respect to Musala.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if he had not been called at all, I would not have objected, but given that he has objected, and presumably because someone thinks he is relevant evidence, I do have some questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you started work in Musala in June of 1992, were you a member of the TO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I think he said that.

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the time, all the units were members of the TO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Are you not receiving any --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I think after Ms. Residovic it was still on Bosnian so I missed that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Were you a member of the military police, sir?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please, I beg your pardon? No, I was never a member of the military police, except in the former army in 1983.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He is a member of the TO. How can he be a member of the --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: MUP, if I understand correctly, MUP is different than the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Sir, is it the case that at some point there were members of the TO that were members of the military police, even if it wasn't you?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: No, the military police, at the time, came from the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Did there ever come a time where the TO or the Bosnian army had military police?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: You indicated you were never a member of the military police. Were any of the people who worked in Musala, to your knowledge, members of the military police?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Military police of the TO?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Is it your testimony, sir, that you don't know whether or not that the guards who worked under you were members of the military police or not?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Do I assume then, sir, have you no idea if Mr. Landzo was ever a member of the military police?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Possibly, but at what time? At what period of time, I don't know, because the first police was formed by the HVO, and who among the Bosniaks was a member of that military police, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: When Mr. Landzo came to Musala to work, do you know if he was a member of the TO or not?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, the whole of Konjic had its pride, and whoever had a uniform, even ladies, they would put them on. And who belonged to the TO in a town or a municipality with 50.000 inhabitants, I know most of those people, but who actually were members, I really don't know. People found their own way to get a hold of weapons, but how the paperwork was done, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Well, sir, my question had specifically to do with the time that Mr. Landzo worked in Musala. Do I understand you that you don't even know during the time he worked for you, you don't even know if Mr. Landzo was a member of the TO or not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, at that time, he was a member of the TO, because all of us who were working at Musala had our military booklets. We started off as the TO. Later on, we became the army, the fourth corps, the sixth corps and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Let me, sir, repeat something that you have answered. During the time that Mr. Landzo worked for you, are you able to say whether or not he was a member of the military police?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Do you see, the question is a little confusing. To begin with, the TO had no military police. Later on, the TO had it's own military police. So be a little bit more clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think he can only confirm he was a member of the TO when he was working with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that when Mr. Landzo worked for you, you don't know if he was a member of the military police or not?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: He couldn't have had two positions at the same time. He could have been a member of the TO or a member of the police. And as he was working with me and Musala, he could only have been a member of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: So it's your understanding, sir, that military police officers are not members of the TO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, you're confusing me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: When you're talking of police, there are two organisations there. The MUP, that is also police; then the military police of the TO. You're referring to a member of the military police of the TO or a member of the TO?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I'm trying to get at.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it the case that, at some point, the TO had its own military police and persons could be military police officers as well as members of the TO? If that's not your understanding, just tell me.

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I understand you fully now. A member of the military police is, at the same time, a member of the TO. And the military police, we know what the assignments are of a military police. I said at the beginning that I was never a member of the military police. I wasn't a member at Musala. If Landzo was with me in the unit, then he, too, was not in the military police, but he was in the TO or the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: You indicated that Mr. Landzo started work in Musala sometime in 1992. Can you give us an approximate date or month when Mr. Landzo started working as a guard in Musala?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't really tell you, but I know that he spent quite a bit of time at Musala.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me then that before he became -- well, let me just ask you. Before he became officially a guard at Musala, would Mr. Landzo sometimes come to Musala?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: While I was in command, he did not, or at least I didn't see him. Really, I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Can you tell us, even within a month or two, when Mr. Landzo started working in Musala?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: It was the summer or maybe even the beginning of the autumn, at the end of the summer, the beginning of the autumn.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Mr. Delic worked in Musala at some point, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Delic never worked at Musala.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: What was your exact title, sir, in Musala?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He was the deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Deputy warden of Musala and head of security.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: You indicated that Mr. Ismet Hebibovic was your superior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: At least until sometime in November of 1992, Mr. Mucic was Mr. Hebibovic's superior, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Until exactly which month, I couldn't say, but he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Do you know approximately what month Mr. Mucic became Mr. Hebibovic's superior?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. You would have to ask Mr. Hebibovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Do you know if it was before or do you know who was Mr. Hebibovic's superior in June of 1992 when you started working at Musala?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: June '92? I'm afraid I couldn't answer that question either.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Who was Mr. Mucic's superior?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. So many commanders changed in Konjic that I really don't know. Let Mr. Mucic tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Sir, how do you know that Mr. Delalic was not Mr. Mucic's superior if you don't know who his superior was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How does that question arise?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic specifically asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I did not put such a question ever. I asked who was the gentleman's superior and whether Mr. Delalic had any connection with Musala. So I object to this kind of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't see the deduction that because he doesn't know whether he was there or not, he must know who was superior? He doesn't have to answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated that there were some prisoners in Musala who had come from Celebici; correct?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Do you know if these persons were considered prisoners of war by the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That calls for a legal conclusion that this court has to make.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if he says he doesn't know, he doesn't know, but I am asking if he knows at the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Suppose he says "yes," would that prove that they are prisoners of war? Suppose he says "no," would that prove that they are prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, but I believe how the Bosnian army viewed them is directly relevant and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If you had some general of the Bosnian army, you could have asked him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we did ask them, and this person worked there. If he doesn't know, he can say he doesn't know, but I certainly am allowed to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He was at a much lower level.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the witness says he doesn't know, certainly I won't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Suppose he says "yes," then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. McHenry, you can leave this question out and ask something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Suppose he says "no," would that prove they are prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated that prisoners were in Musala to protect them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Can you just explain what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I'll try. Whether you will understand me, I don't know. The prisoners were placed there for the following reason. After all, that was the beginning of the aggression. All the media were reporting on rapes, killings, expulsions, and so on. Let me avoid enumerating all the details. Many people from Konjic came from municipalities managing to escape the knife, the bullet, or the shell. When they came there, they wanted to go in and beat the prisoners. Can that be of assistance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think it should be. It's for protective custody, and the whole municipality was against them.

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: I assume that these persons who were detained, they weren't free to go? They weren't free to leave Musala, were they?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: No, they could not leave. They were not allowed to leave Musala for reasons I've already stated.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Did those reasons have to do with the fact that you said that they were carrying arms, or did it have to do with your desire to protect the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, all the detainees who were kept at Musala were caught with weapons on them. The Serbs who lived in Konjic, who stayed in Konjic, many of them didn't take weapons, and they still lived there. Many people who were there in the camp, they still come to Konjic. Every day they are coming to Konjic, even now.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: You indicated that sometimes when you were at Musala, you went to the frontline, and sometimes Mr. Landzo went with you. How frequently did Mr. Landzo go to the frontlines with you, approximately?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the precise number. I said it twice. Whenever I asked for volunteers, Mr. Landzo, whom I can see here, volunteered, together with some others who, unfortunately, are dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: At the frontline, what did Mr. Landzo do?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I see, Madam, that you don't know what the frontline is. On the frontline, you have trenches; you have machine guns. Mr. Landzo, who was in charge of a place, either in the winter or in the summer, he had to spend two to six hours there watching enemy trenches so that we were not surprised by the enemy. And he had to shoot if necessary and kill.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: So he shot. Did he ever help dig trenches or did he just keep guard and shoot if necessary?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course all the trenches were dug by ourselves and by the local people.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Do you remember whether or not Mr. Landzo ever helped dig a trench?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the relevance on this.

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I can't see the relevance of whether he dug a trench or not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I already told you that I can't tell you. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Can you remember anything he did besides stand and watch and then sometimes shoot?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: What are you referring to, "shoot, watch"?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: You indicated that one of the things he would do would be to watch the enemy trenches?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand you now. Of course, he would shoot. I shot too and killed too to save my family, my house. You would do the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not questioning what you did on the frontline. I'm just asking you, in addition to that, did you ever see Mr. Landzo do any other activities?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Such as?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Such as deliver reinforcements, deliver weapons to someone in another position, march with you from one position to another?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: No, he did not. Short distances, yes. Mostly we had the first battalion on the left bank of the Neretva. We organised transportation to about 500 metres from the frontline.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: When Mr. Landzo went to the frontline, would he usually get special transportation?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Mostly he did. It hardly ever happened that we had no transportation. I can even give you the name of the driver if you are interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: No, that's fine. Did you ever have any conversation with Mr. Landzo about anything to do with Celebici prison?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: No, because I'm not interested in it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Did you even know that Mr. Landzo had ever worked in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I was told by others, or everybody that came from there said that he was there with them. Some dozen of them were transported, together with Broceta, to where I was. My superior, he said that Esad was with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Did you ever hear any reports that detainees were mistreated while in Celebici? I'm talking about in 1992. Did you ever hear any reports that detainees were mistreated in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. I heard about the murder of Keljo and Klimenta and nothing else, and one of our fighters.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Was it in 1992 that you heard about the murder of Mr. Klimenta or was it later?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992 or at the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Do you know why certain detainees were kept in Celebici and certain detainees were in Musala?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: No, that wasn't my area. I wasn't in charge of thinking about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Sometimes detainees would be brought to Musala from Celebici and you had no idea why. I'm just making sure I understood you.

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: They were brought from there. I don't know for what reason. Really, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Now, did you yourself ever see Mr. Mucic at Musala in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I think once or twice, I'm not sure exactly, but once or twice.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: On the occasions when you saw Mr. Mucic in Musala in 1992, what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mucic came once. I don't know exactly the number of times he came. He brought some certificates and he released a large number of detainees.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: Was there any other time that you saw him there?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did Mr. Mucic ever give any instructions concerning how the prisoners in Musala were to be treated?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. As far as I know, the warden doesn't know either, but he may know it better than me.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY
utterances.text: You talked about Mico Kuljanin. Why did Mico Kuljanin have special privileges in Musala, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SENADIN TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Why he had special privileges, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to have some redirect. I wonder if I could just request a short break to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: No, if you are not ready, we will adjourn until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I thought we could finish with him today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I thought so but it appears --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: I spent time to get the witnesses and go back and forth, so I just need a short break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You can get more tidier tomorrow morning and then know how to organise your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the registry and I have worked out the fact that Dr. Verde will testify without an Italian interpreter in the morning. So we will proceed with Dr. Verde testifying in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Following the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes. It won't take long, I'm sure. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will now rise and reassemble tomorrow at 10.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: 6.15 p.m. to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 14th day of July, 1998 at 10.00 a.m.
